did: I built the phone's half of Game Week Bites' live game day. The recorder now gets home's live offers over a socket while Game day is open on the paired phone, and says plainly when home is out of reach, not following games, or needs an app update. Each bite also keeps home's clock against the phone's. The socket's logic is a small state machine with tests for every stale event, and two independent reviews found real gaps that I fixed: a phone clock off by days would have had every bite refused, and off the home network the screen used to say it was still asking. I also prepared the held ledger change for the server's bite-to-play matcher, and answered what Before and After mean for its chains.

calls.title: The game day socket widens the one-door rule for reaching home
options: Widen LA8 and LA1 for one WebSocket file, as built
Keep native HTTP alone and poll a route for live offers
calls.why: You chose a WebSocket on Oct 25 and said to go with the recommended on Nov 13; native HTTP cannot carry a socket.
calls.undo: Replace the live socket with a feed that polls a home route, drop LA21, and restore LA8 and LA1.

calls.title: An unreadable-message close from home means the app needs an update
options: Treat it as home out of reach and keep retrying
calls.why: Home closes with 4400 for a stale sequence number, which the phone now repairs at once, or for a message it cannot read, which retrying cannot fix.
calls.undo: Map 4400 back to 'away' in live-model.ts so it retries.

calls.title: The bite matcher runs as its own task, beside the game feed
options: Inside the game feed's worker, amending GF4
A separate task that alone reads bites and writes matches
calls.why: It keeps the feed's worker free of anything about a person, as GF4 says; you said to go with the recommended.
calls.undo: Call the matcher from the feed's pass, amend GF4, and fold the bite-matched ledger family into game-feed.

left: Nobody has tried the live socket on a real phone yet: whether the WebView trusts home's certificate and the proxy passes the socket through is still to see.
A phone whose pairing home ended while the socket was closed reads as home out of reach and keeps retrying while Game day is open; the page can't tell that refusal from no answer.
GWB7, matching each bite to its play, is the server session's; its ledger placement (#2921) waits as a draft to merge just before the server PR.
